questions.query: why does generator maximize log D(G(z)) instead
questions.reference: Early in training D rejects samples confidently, so log(1 − D(G(z))) saturates; maximizing log D(G(z)) gives the same fixed point but much stronger gradients early on.

questions.query: how does vit turn an image into tokens
questions.reference: The image is reshaped into N flattened P x P patches, linearly projected to D dimensions, prepended with a learnable [class] embedding and added to position embeddings.
Standard learnable 1D position embeddings; 2D-aware embeddings gave no significant gains.

questions.query: why does vit need large datasets
questions.reference: ViT has much less image-specific inductive bias than CNNs (locality, 2D neighbourhood structure, translation equivariance), so it needs large-scale pretraining such as ImageNet-21k or JFT-300M to outperform them.

questions.query: how does self attention compute weights
questions.reference: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(Q K^T / sqrt(d_k)) V: compatibility scores are dot products of queries and keys, scaled and normalized by softmax to weight the values.
